title: More Canadians Visit the U.S., but Many Still Stay Away

paragraphs: Canadians are traveling to the United States again, but slowly. In September, Canadian return trips from the U.S. rose 6.8% compared with a year earlier, according to Statistics Canada. A return trip is counted when a Canadian comes home after a visit to the United States. September was the sixth consecutive month of growth. The agency released the numbers on Tuesday.

Trips by car went up 5.6%, and trips by plane went up 11.6%. That sounds like good news for American hotels, shops and airlines that welcome Canadian tourists. But the growth starts from a very low level.

Compared with September 2024, the picture looks very different. Car trips were 31.1% lower than two years ago. Trips by air were down 18.7%. In other words, many Canadians who used to visit their southern neighbor have not come back.

The same pattern appears in many places, both near the border and far from it. In northern New England, crossings were up 6% from last year but down 23% from 2024. In Whatcom County, Washington, cars going south rose 3% but stayed 27% below 2024. Even Hawaii, a popular winter destination, saw only a slight rise of 0.6% in Canadian arrivals. It is still 4% below 2024.

Business travel is doing better than vacation travel. Corporate Traveller Canada said flights booked across the border were up 2.2% in September. For the year so far, they were 3.9% higher than in 2024. Flight Centre Canada said vacation travel is growing from an unusually weak 2025, so it still has a long way to recover.

Interest is growing online, too. The travel website FlightHub said searches for U.S. destinations rose 15% from a year earlier, even though airline ticket prices jumped 17%. So many Canadians are clearly still thinking about a trip.

Still, many Canadians have strong feelings about their neighbor. There is also tension over trade between the two countries. In a Leger survey of 1,538 Canadian adults, 60% said they were less open to U.S. travel than at any point in the past year. And 43% said that ending the trade tension between Canada and the U.S. would not change how likely they are to visit.

For U.S. tourism, the direction is good. Six consecutive months of growth is a steady trend, and tourists from Canada are slowly coming back. But each step is slight, and tourism needs a steady recovery for many more months to recover fully. The road back to 2024 levels still looks long.
